log: Member was referred to as being "behind a closed door" and corrected it — she is out on the floor, not shut away, and does not know which is worse: her mother's disappearing or her own performing fine all day then crying in the car.
Member's charge nurse reviewed her charting with her line by line on Friday and was nice about it, which made it worse.

Member spent Saturday morning in the parish kitchen and it was a good morning; she did not notice until later, when she caught herself laughing for real at an old parish lady's story about her grandson and checked herself, as if asking whether being happy was allowed.
Member does not trust a good morning to mean anything yet and wants to know whether Saturday meant anything or whether she will be "behind like this for good."
Member stayed forty minutes late on Friday to catch up the charting and did not write the time down; she said it was just paperwork and pushed back on reading it as about being seen.
Member's charge nurse wants the charting caught up by end of next week.

At Sunday dinner at her mother's (twelve people), her mother told the sinigang story twice, same pot, and everyone laughed both times; the second time Member watched her mother's hands, same order, fish then tamarind, and could not remember whether her dad told the story before or after her mother.
Member dismissed the gap in placing her dad in the memory as "just how memory goes."
Member pushed back when the counsellor answered a question with a question, calling it a circle, and accepted the honest answer that the laughing is still available to her even if not fixed.
Member describes sitting at the station with the charge nurse as feeling about eight years old, over what is just boxes that need filling in.
[open] Member has the charting to do next week and named it as a thing she has to just do.
Member is being picked up by Dan and had to leave the session early.
